In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the immunopathological changes in five different mouse strains infected with P. berghei.
the immunopathological mechanisms of malaria.
the study of the pathogenesis of cerebral malaria, the immunological mechanisms involved, the development of new drugs and the study of the immunopathology of other tissue lesions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cerebral lesions are a major factor in the pathogenesis of acute deaths in the P. berghei model.
the histopathological findings in the cerebral lesions in this study are consistent with the findings in the cerebral malaria in humans.
the immunopathology of cerebral malaria is a complex and multifactorial event.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the immunopathology of cerebral lesions in this malaria model is related to the strain of mouse, to the parasite strain used and to the time after infection.
the immunopathology of cerebral malaria in this model is related to the strain-dependent development of the disease.
the A/J mice were more susceptible to the infection than BALB/c, C57B/L, CBA and OF1.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immunopathology of malaria in mice is complex.
the immune response in the brain is very important for the outcome of infection.
the immune response is not the only factor that determines the severity of the disease.
